rounds.text: Tirupati Foam Ltd presents a compelling value case as it trades at a modest price-to-book ratio of 0.99x against a sector benchmark of 1.95x, sitting near the lower end of its 52-week range [E2, E5, E7]. The business demonstrates robust cash generation with a cash conversion ratio of 2.50x, delivering Rs 5 Cr in both operating and free cash flow for March 2026 [E33, E35]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 120 per share, offering a substantial 36.2% margin of safety over the current market price of Rs 76.7 [E42, E43]. The company's recent operational performance shows accelerating momentum, highlighted by a net profit growth of 62% year-over-year and a results score of 98/100, while insider alignment remains solid with promoters increasing their stake to 71.72% [E40, E56, E59]. Conceded: the company carries a leveraged debt-to-equity ratio of 1.09x and has delivered a low median return on equity of 6% over the last three years [E27, E37].

Tirupati Foam Ltd suffers from structural growth stagnation, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of just 2% [E14] and a negative 3-year sales contraction of -2% [E16], culminating in a -4% decline over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Profitability is equally lackluster, characterized by a persistent low return on equity stuck at 6% over the last 1, 3, and 5 years [E26, E27, E28, E52], severely trailing sector benchmarks [E9]. The company carries tangible balance sheet and operational vulnerabilities, notably a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.09x where debt exceeds net worth [E37], alongside a flagged low interest coverage ratio [E50] and a quarterly operating-margin trend that has been steadily decreasing over the last four quarters [E32]. Market sentiment reflects these underlying weaknesses, leaving the stock languishing at just 26% of its 52-week range [E5] alongside a sharp 1-year share price collapse of -37% [E24]. Conceded: the company maintains a healthy dividend payout of 21.7% [E49] and exhibits strong short-term cash generation with operating cash flow reaching Rs 5 Cr and covering reported profit by 2.50x in Mar 2026 [E33, E34].

Conceded: 10-year compounded sales growth is 2% [E14] and 3-year sales growth is -2% [E16]. However, the bear overlooks a powerful operational turnaround: recent quarterly metrics reveal surging top and bottom lines with net profit up 62% YoY and sales up 22% YoY, signalling that stale multi-year averages completely miss the company's accelerating trajectory [E54, E56, E59]. While ROE stands at 6% [E28], the stock trades at a deep discount of just 0.99x price-to-book and 14.88x P/E compared to sector benchmarks of 1.95x and 25.33x, making low returns more than adequately priced in [E2, E6, E7]. Conceded: debt-to-equity is 1.09x [E37], but total borrowings actually decreased from Rs 40 Cr to Rs 37 Cr while generating robust free cash flow of Rs 5 Cr and a 2.50x cash conversion ratio that fully backs profits with hard cash [E33, E35, E38]. Although quarterly margins show a recent decrease [E32], the discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 120 offering a 36.2% margin of safety from today's price [E42, E43], and the bear's cited 37% share price collapse [E24] is simply an overreaction creating an exceptional entry point for a fundamentally improving business backed by rising promoter stakes of 71.72% [E40, E45].

Conceded: recent figures show net profit up 62% YoY and sales up 22% YoY [E56, E54]. However, pointing to these short-term bursts ignores the multi-year reality where 10-year compounded sales growth limps at 2% and 3-year sales growth contracts by -2% [E14, E16]. The bull claims low returns are priced in via a 0.99x price-to-book ratio [E2], but this ignores the persistent low ROE of 6% over the last 3, 5, and 10 years [E25, E26, E27], alongside an officially flagged low interest coverage ratio [E50] and a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.09x where debt exceeds net worth [E37]. Conceded: borrowings decreased to Rs 37 Cr [E38] and DCF outputs an intrinsic value of Rs 120 [E42]. Yet, the quarterly operating-margin trend reads strictly Decreasing over the last four quarters [E32], and the company is saddled with a poor 5-year sales growth of 5.25% [E51] while its share price has deteriorated by 37% over the past year [E24].
